stem: The school health programme (SHP) is best described as which of the following?
options: A coordinated, multidisciplinary programme designed to promote, protect, and maintain the health of schoolchildren and school personnel
A single, isolated vaccination event held once per academic year
A purely administrative budgeting exercise with no health component
A programme limited strictly to dental care, excluding all other health domains

stem: The Federal Republic of Nigeria (FRN, 2006) views the aim of the school health programme as extending beyond the individual to which broader level?
options: National development
Only the individual household's finances
Only the private school sector's profitability
Only the teacher's personal career advancement

stem: According to the Nigerian Federal Ministry of Education (2006), the school health programme is a strategic tool for achieving which set of goals, alongside Health for All (HFA)?
options: Education for All (EFA), health-related Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), NEEDS, the Universal Basic Education Act, and goals of the National Policy on Education (NPE)
Only goals related to international trade tariffs
Only goals related to national currency stabilization
Only goals related to military defense spending

stem: According to the EFA Framework rationale, improved health and nutrition status among students is linked to which school-related outcomes?
options: Improved enrolment and retention, and reduced absenteeism
Reduced need for any teacher training whatsoever
Increased classroom overcrowding
Reduced need for school infrastructure maintenance

stem: The EFA Framework rationale also notes that health promotion for teachers benefits their health, morale, and which other outcome?
options: Quality of instruction
Only their personal investment portfolio
Only their eligibility for early retirement
Only their seniority ranking within the school hierarchy

stem: According to the EFA Framework rationale, health education is MOST effective when delivered using which approach?
options: Interactive methods in a skill-based approach
Purely passive lecture format with no learner interaction
Written memoranda distributed with no discussion
Entirely unsupervised, self-directed reading with no facilitation

stem: Among the reasons justifying special attention to school health programmes, school children are described as an important population segment because the nation's survival and future prosperity depend on which of the following?
options: This segment of the population
Only the retired population segment
Only the adult working population aged over 50
Only the segment employed in agriculture

stem: Children at school age are described as constantly undergoing major physical and emotional development, which calls for which type of service?
options: An effective and well-planned service within the school and community
No service at all, since development is assumed to occur automatically
A service limited strictly to physical education classes
A service limited strictly to examination preparation

stem: School age is described as a period when children are still amenable to new ideas, offering a unique opportunity to do what, with an influence that extends to their parents at home?
options: Impart basic knowledge of disease causation and control
Impart advanced university-level coursework exclusively
Impart only vocational trade skills unrelated to health
Impart only foreign language instruction unrelated to health

stem: Among the AIMS of the school health programme, which statement reflects the ultimate purpose of ensuring every child is as fit as possible?
options: So that each child may obtain the maximum benefit from his or her education
So that the school can reduce its total enrolment numbers
So that the school can increase tuition fees without objection
So that the school can reduce the number of teachers employed

stem: According to the aims of the school health programme, why is it insufficient to simply check that no disease exists?
options: Because there must be a definite programme designed to make every child acquire positive health habits and knowledge, such as personal hygiene
Because disease-checking is entirely unnecessary and should be discontinued
Because only teachers, never health workers, should be involved in health checks
Because health habits are assumed to be inherited and cannot be taught

stem: Among the aims of the school health programme, arrangements should be made for the ascertainment and treatment of which groups of children?
options: Various groups of handicapped children, such as the blind, partially sighted, deaf, physically handicapped, educationally subnormal, maladjusted, and epileptic
Only children who have already achieved perfect academic scores
Only children belonging to the wealthiest households in the community
Only children who have never experienced any illness

stem: Which principle of an effective school health programme addresses the child's physical, mental, emotional, social, nutritional, and environmental health together?
options: Comprehensive care
Accessibility
Confidentiality
Cultural appropriateness

stem: Which principle of school health programme places emphasis on preventing disease and promoting health, rather than concentrating only on treatment?
options: Prevention and health promotion
Child-centred care
Continuity of care
Referral and follow-up

stem: Which principle of school health programme requires that services be appropriate to the child's age, developmental level, abilities, and culture?
options: Child-centred care
Multidisciplinary collaboration
Family and community participation
Confidentiality

stem: Which principle of school health programme requires that services be continuous and linked with appropriate health facilities?
options: Continuity of care
Confidentiality
Child-centred care
Family and community participation

stem: Which principle of school health programme emphasises that different professionals should work together to address the complex health needs of children?
options: Multidisciplinary collaboration
Cultural appropriateness
Accessibility
Confidentiality

stem: Which principle of school health programme requires that information obtained about a child's health be handled appropriately and shared only when necessary for the child's welfare?
options: Confidentiality
Accessibility
Cultural appropriateness
Multidisciplinary collaboration

stem: Which principle of school health programme requires that health interventions consider the beliefs, practices, and socioeconomic circumstances of the community?
options: Cultural appropriateness
Referral and follow-up
Comprehensive care
Continuity of care

stem: The Nigerian National School Health Policy (2006) identifies how many components of the school health programme?
options: Five
Two
Ten
Twenty

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as one of the five components of the school health programme under the Nigerian National School Health Policy (2006)?
options: Healthful School Environment
International Currency Exchange Management
Municipal Road Construction
National Defense Policy

stem: School health services are best described as which of the following?
options: Preventive and curative health services provided at the school for learners and school staff, with a view to protecting, promoting, and maintaining their health
A service that exists solely to generate school revenue
A service limited strictly to annual sports day first aid
A purely theoretical concept with no operational service delivery

stem: Although school health services comprise both preventive and curative approaches, emphasis must be placed on which of the two?
options: Preventive efforts, rather than curative efforts
Curative efforts exclusively, with no preventive component
Neither approach, since both are considered equally unimportant
Only curative efforts for communicable diseases, never non-communicable ones

stem: According to the WHO's Expert Committee on Comprehensive School Health Education and Promotion, what do children need in order to learn effectively?
options: Good health
Only advanced textbooks regardless of health status
Only extended school hours regardless of health status
Only a larger teacher-to-student ratio regardless of health status

stem: According to Ogundele (2002), the focus and emphasis of school health services includes identification of school members' health needs and which other related step?
options: Appropriate selection and utilization of responsive health services to meet those needs
Elimination of all health services from the school budget
Exclusive reliance on parental self-diagnosis with no professional involvement
Permanent exclusion of children with identified health needs from school

stem: Among the focus areas of school health services per Ogundele (2002), control of communicable diseases should have which strategy at the centre of control efforts?
options: Prevention
Mass expulsion of affected children with no treatment
Permanent school closure at the first sign of any illness
Exclusive reliance on curative treatment with no preventive measures

stem: Besides promoting health and preventing disease, which other objective of school health services relates specifically to detection?
options: Promote early detection of defects and diagnosis of diseases amongst all school community members
Promote delayed detection of defects until adulthood
Eliminate all diagnostic screening from the school setting
Restrict detection services exclusively to teaching staff, excluding learners

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a service to be provided to school children, related to the school surroundings?
options: Promotion of optimal sanitary conditions in the school environment
Promotion of increased classroom overcrowding
Promotion of unrestricted access to hazardous chemicals on school grounds
Promotion of unsupervised access to the school's electrical systems

stem: Besides Health Appraisal and Health Observation, which other activities are listed among the components of school health services?
options: Medical Health Examination and Health Screening, First Aid and Emergency Care, and Health History and Record
Only classroom decoration and bulletin board design
Only school uniform tailoring and alteration
Only inter-school sports tournament scheduling

stem: Health appraisal is best described as which of the following?
options: That aspect of health services which concerns itself with evaluating the health of an individual objectively
A purely subjective, unstructured opinion with no evaluative component
A process limited strictly to measuring a child's shoe size
A process conducted only once in a child's entire school career

stem: Health observation is best described as which of the following?
options: Consciously examining the physical and emotional health and well-being of school children to establish whether there is deviation from normal health status
A process that requires highly specialized, expensive equipment in every instance
A process that can only be performed by a radiologist
A process limited strictly to measuring blood pressure with specialized equipment

stem: According to the material, who can observe the health status of a child through health observation, though closer attention leading to screening may fall to trained professionals?
options: Anybody, though closer screening may be the duty of trained professionals like doctors or school nurses
Only a fully licensed physician, with no role for anyone else
Only the child's parent, with no role for school staff
Only a hospital administrator, with no role for clinical staff

stem: During periodic teacher inspection as part of health observation, which specific findings should prompt referral to the school health centre?
options: Discharge in the ears/eyes, squint, unusual colour of eyes, inability to see the blackboard, inability to hear or read properly, and skin rashes
A child's preference for a particular subject
A child's choice of favourite colour
A child's handwriting style

stem: As part of health observation, teachers should measure the heights and weights of children at which point, with results sent to the school health clinic within how many hours?
options: At the beginning of every school term, with results sent within 48 hours
Only once, at the child's final year of schooling, with no time limit for reporting
Daily, with results sent within 5 minutes
Only when a child requests it, with no defined reporting timeframe

stem: Medical/dental health examination and screening are conducted in which TWO forms?
options: Pre-enrolment/pre-employment stage and periodic medical examination/health screening
Only at graduation, with no earlier screening at all
Only during school holidays, with no screening during term time
Only for teaching staff, excluding all learners

stem: Besides school children, pre-employment medical/dental examination should also be conducted for which other members of the school community?
options: All other members of the school community, including food handlers
Only the school's financial administrators
Only visiting dignitaries attending school events
Only parents attending parent-teacher meetings

stem: Which category of personnel should conduct pre-entry medical screening, according to the implementation guideline?
options: Trained health personnel
Untrained volunteers with no health background
Only the school's security staff
Only the school's bursar

stem: Dental/oral health screening, as a preventive and appraisal measure, should be done at the school health services centre by a dentist at which interval?
options: Every six months
Every ten years
Only once, at the child's birth
Only after the child has already left school

stem: Regular de-worming exercise, as part of routine screening, should be done at which minimum interval?
options: At least once every 3 months
At least once every 10 years
Only once in a child's entire lifetime
Only when a child specifically requests it

stem: First aid and emergency care in the school setting is given for which specific purpose?
options: To reduce pain and complications, and to prevent the injury from growing worse before proper medical attention is given
To replace the need for any further medical attention entirely
To delay all medical attention indefinitely
To be administered only by a fully qualified surgeon on site

stem: According to the material, who should be trained in basic first aid and emergency care skills within the school setting?
options: Both staff and learners
Only the school's most senior administrator
Only learners, excluding all staff
No one, since first aid is said to require no training

stem: If a learner transfers to another school, what happens to their original health record, according to the material?
options: The original health record is expected to go with the learner, while the duplicate is retained by the original school
The original record is destroyed immediately upon transfer
The original record remains permanently with the original school, with no copy transferred
No health record is required to be transferred or retained under any circumstance

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as content that the health record should contain?
options: Personal and family history, history of past illnesses/hospitalization, records of immunization, and records of screening tests
Only the child's favourite extracurricular activity
Only the names of the child's classmates
Only the child's examination timetable for the current term

stem: According to the material, each entry into a student's health record must be dated and authenticated by the staff member making the entry, indicating which specific details?
options: Name, age, and sex
Only the staff member's favourite subject to teach
Only the staff member's home address
Only the staff member's preferred mode of transportation

stem: According to the material, what might happen if young people have no opportunities to obtain coping skills through health counselling?
options: They might resort to seeking information from friends and other platforms that may not provide health-supportive solutions
They will automatically develop coping skills without any external input
They will be permanently exempted from all further schooling
They will immediately be referred to a tertiary hospital regardless of the issue

stem: Health education, as a component of school health services, is described as entailing which of the following?
options: Empowering individuals and groups with functional knowledge required to stimulate positive attitudes needed to adopt health-promoting behaviours
Simply distributing pamphlets with no further engagement
Restricting health information exclusively to teaching staff
Replacing all curative services with education alone, eliminating treatment entirely

stem: Why do communicable diseases pose MORE threat than non-communicable diseases within the school setting, according to the material?
options: Because the presence of many people in the school makes transmission possible and easy, and learners can transport disease to different communities
Because communicable diseases are the only type of disease that can ever occur in a school
Because non-communicable diseases are entirely absent from the school-age population
Because communicable diseases cannot be prevented under any circumstances

stem: In controlling communicable diseases within the school setting, which prevention strategy is described as most preferred?
options: Primary prevention
Tertiary prevention exclusively, with no role for primary prevention
No prevention strategy at all, relying solely on treatment after illness occurs
Secondary prevention exclusively, with no role for primary prevention

stem: The school is described as an important setting for vaccination and immunization, particularly during which circumstance?
options: The outbreak of a disease
Only during the final week of the academic year
Only during the school's annual sports day
Only during parent-teacher conference week

stem: Regarding supervision of food vendors in schools, which of the following should be monitored to prevent foodborne illness?
options: Personal hygiene of food handlers, cleanliness of food preparation areas, and safe water supply
Only the price charged for food items
Only the colour scheme of the food vendor's uniform
Only the vendor's seniority within the school community

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed among the common health problems of school-age children?
options: Rheumatic heart disease
Age-related macular degeneration, which affects only the elderly
Benign prostatic hyperplasia, which affects only older men
Osteoarthritis of the hip, which affects only the elderly

stem: Besides rheumatic heart disease and malaria, which other condition is explicitly listed as a common health problem of school-age children, particularly relevant in some populations?
options: Anaemia, especially sickle cell anaemia
Age-related cataract requiring immediate surgery in every case
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from decades of smoking
Benign prostatic hyperplasia

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a major responsibility of the school nurse?
options: Conducting or coordinating health assessments and identifying children requiring further care
Setting the school's final examination questions
Managing the school's financial accounts exclusively
Determining the school's academic curriculum content

stem: The school nurse's role in 'environmental health' includes identifying environmental hazards and advocating for which of the following?
options: Safe water, sanitation, ventilation, lighting, waste disposal, and food hygiene
Increased use of untreated water sources
Reduced ventilation to conserve energy regardless of air quality
Unregulated waste disposal to reduce costs

stem: Which member of the school health team is specifically responsible for medical examination, diagnosis, treatment, supervision, and referral?
options: The medical practitioner
The environmental health officer
The radiographer
The nutritionist/dietitian

stem: Which member of the school health team provides nutritional assessment, counselling, and dietary intervention?
options: The nutritionist/dietitian
The radiographer
The environmental health officer
The psychologist/counsellor

stem: Which member of the school health team assesses sanitation, water supply, food hygiene, waste disposal, and environmental hazards?
options: The environmental health officer
The dentist
The medical practitioner
The parent/guardian

stem: Parents and guardians, as members of the school health team, are expected to provide relevant health information and do what else regarding decisions about the child's health?
options: Participate in decisions concerning the child's health
Be entirely excluded from any decision-making process
Delegate all decision-making exclusively to the school principal
Have no role whatsoever once the child is enrolled in school

stem: School administrators, teachers, and community leaders are described as being in a unique position to identify the health needs and problems of children for which reason?
options: By virtue of their proximity to the school
Because they have formal medical training exceeding that of physicians
Because they are legally required to diagnose disease independently
Because they have no connection to the children's daily environment

stem: Among the prerequisites for a healthful school, what must be available at all times for emergency situations?
options: A first aid box
A fully equipped operating theatre
An on-site pharmacy stocked with controlled substances
A dedicated ambulance fleet owned by the school

stem: Among the prerequisites for a healthful school, what type of support must the headmaster give to children and teachers to make school health activities successful?
options: Both financial and moral support
Only verbal encouragement with no financial commitment
Only financial support with no moral or motivational engagement
No support of any kind, since activities are expected to be self-sustaining

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as an ADVANTAGE of school health programmes/services?
options: It helps to identify abnormalities promptly among pupils and to give immediate treatment
It guarantees elimination of all disease from the general population
It eliminates the need for any hospital services nationwide
It replaces the need for any parental involvement in a child's health

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a factor that influences the health of school children in developing countries?
options: Socioeconomic factors
The international exchange rate of a completely unrelated foreign currency
The school's choice of academic calendar colour scheme
The brand of stationery used by the school administration

stem: Besides genetic, environmental, and socioeconomic factors, which other factors are listed as influencing the health of school children in developing countries?
options: Health service factors, communicable diseases, and ignorance of parents
Only factors related to international space exploration funding
Only factors related to global shipping container logistics
Only factors related to unrelated agricultural commodity futures trading

stem: Besides PTAs and grants-in-aid, which other activities are listed as sources of funds for school health programmes?
options: Prize-giving day/graduation ceremony, inter-house competitions, and quiz/debate/drama competitions
Only unrelated international arbitration settlements
Only unrelated foreign direct investment in unrelated industries
Only unrelated cryptocurrency mining operations

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A school nurse notices during routine teacher-reported health observation that a 9-year-old has a persistent white-reflex-free but markedly reduced ability to read the blackboard, along with a chronic discharge from one ear, and the child's growth chart shows a sudden drop in weight percentile since the last termly measurement. The nurse also recalls the child's health record shows incomplete immunization. Which combination of actions reflects the correct application of health appraisal, health observation, and record-keeping principles?
options: Refer the child promptly for visual and ENT screening at the school health centre, investigate the weight drop as a possible nutritional or communicable disease indicator, update and complete the immunization record, and ensure all findings are dated and authenticated in the child's health record
Ignore the findings since classroom teachers have no legitimate role in identifying health problems
Withhold referral until the child personally requests it, since referral services are optional for school-age children
Discard the old health record entirely rather than update it, since incomplete records cannot legally be amended

stem: CASE SCENARIO: During a disease outbreak in a community, the school health team conducts mass immunization at the school, while simultaneously identifying and referring children with early signs of the illness, and the school nurse manages minor related ailments within her scope using approved standing orders, only referring severe cases to hospital. Which principle BEST explains why this layered approach helps decongest hospitals, consistent with the stated advantages of school health programmes?
options: Because immunization prevents disease, minor ailments are managed on-site, and only serious cases requiring specialist care are referred, reducing unnecessary hospital burden
Because all cases, regardless of severity, must always be referred to hospital to decongest the school clinic
Because immunization during outbreaks is never appropriate and should be deferred until the outbreak ends
Because the school nurse has no authority to manage any ailment, however minor, without physician countersignature

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A rural school serves a community with low socioeconomic status, limited access to safe water, high rates of childhood anaemia including sickle cell disease, and a shortage of trained health personnel. The PTA proposes funding a school health initiative through proceeds from prize-giving day, inter-house sports, and a quiz competition, while also pushing for improved sanitation facilities as part of a healthful school environment. Which combination of factors and interventions BEST reflects the material's framework for addressing child health in developing-country school settings?
options: Socioeconomic status, health service availability, and environmental conditions are recognised influencing factors, and community-generated funding alongside environmental improvements (sanitation, safe water) are appropriate, complementary responses
Socioeconomic and environmental factors have no documented relationship to school children's health in developing countries
PTA fundraising activities are explicitly prohibited as a source of funds for school health programmes
Sanitation and water supply are unrelated to the scope of a healthful school environment and should not be prioritised by the PTA

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A newly blind adolescent who lost his sight following untreated severe trachoma with trichiasis is enrolled in a community-based rehabilitation programme, where he receives health counselling for emotional adjustment, his family is educated on avoiding both overprotection and neglect, and he is later referred for vocational assessment, while health education sessions emphasize hygiene and early care-seeking to protect other children in the school from similar outcomes. Which combination of school health service components is illustrated here?
options: Health counselling, referral services, and health education are being used together to address an individual's rehabilitation needs while also preventing similar outcomes in other learners
Only health education is relevant here, since counselling and referral are not recognised components of school health services
Rehabilitation and vocational assessment fall entirely outside the scope of any school health service component
Family education about overprotection and neglect is unrelated to any principle of school health service delivery

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A school food vendor is found by the environmental health officer to have poor personal hygiene and is preparing food near an unsafe water source, while several children have recently presented with gastrointestinal symptoms. The school nurse coordinates with the environmental health officer, the medical practitioner, and the teacher to address the situation, applying the principle that communicable disease control in schools should prioritise one particular level of prevention. Which combination of actions and principle BEST reflects appropriate multidisciplinary response?
options: The vendor's hygiene and water source are corrected per public health regulations, affected children are assessed and treated, and primary prevention (hygiene, safe water, supervision) is prioritised going forward, coordinated through the multidisciplinary school health team
The vendor should continue operating unchanged, since food vendor supervision is outside the scope of school health services
Only curative treatment of affected children is appropriate, with no attention to the vendor's hygiene or water source
Multidisciplinary collaboration is unnecessary, since environmental health officers have no legitimate role in food vendor supervision
